name: uk.co.alama/wardrobe
title: Alama Wardrobe
description: Your wardrobe in ChatGPT and Claude: what to wear, what suits you, try-on on your own photo.

tools.name: whoami
tools.description: The signed-in Alama account: username, display name and how many items and outfits it holds.

tools.name: get_context
tools.description: Start here. One bounded summary of the signed-in person: their wardrobe in numbers (garments per class, main colours, materials, formality) with the garments they use most, their written style profile, what the wardrobe is missing, their usual sizes, what they have recently worn, liked or rejected, and what they want. detail='summary' (default, under 2,500 tokens) is enough for most conversations; 'full' (under 8,000) adds the evidence behind each profile line and more garments. Use the garment ids with get_item. Call it once per conversation, not per message.

tools.name: style_profile
tools.description: The signed-in person's style profile as Alama has written it from their wardrobe and what they wear: a short summary, one line each on palette, shapes, formality, materials and most-worn pieces, their style words, what they avoid and their usual sizes. Use it to answer 'what do you know about my style' or before recommending anything. Lines marked confirmed_by_person are in the person's own words. It is a description, not a rule: say so if the person disagrees, and tell them they can correct it in the Alama app.

tools.name: list_wardrobe
tools.description: The signed-in person's own clothes, most recently updated first, with category, colour, size, material, formality and warmth. Filter by category: a garment class ('tops', 'bottoms', 'dresses', 'outerwear', 'shoes', 'bags', 'hats', 'accessories') finds every item of that kind whatever its category is called, and any other word matches the category name (e.g. 'jeans', 'knitwear'). Also filter by colour, formality ('loungewear', 'casual', 'athletic', 'smart_casual', 'business', 'formal'), warmth ('very_light', 'light', 'medium', 'warm', 'very_warm'), favourites, or a word in the name. Paged: pass `next_cursor` back as `cursor`. For an overview, call get_context first: it is one call instead of several pages.

tools.name: get_item
tools.description: One item from the signed-in person's wardrobe by id, with a one-hour link to its picture. An item without a photo comes with `add_photo_url` instead: a one-hour link where the person adds one.

tools.name: suggest_outfit
tools.description: Put together one outfit from the signed-in person's own clothes for an occasion, the weather or a date. Returns the chosen items with pictures and a short rationale. Nothing is saved. Free accounts get a daily allowance; Organiser and Style Pass are unlimited.

tools.name: does_it_suit_me
tools.description: Whether a product the person is looking at suits them, judged against their own wardrobe and style profile. Pass the product page link, a link to its picture, or its description (pass the description too when you have it: some shops refuse to show their pages to servers). Returns a verdict (suits you, could work, a stretch, not for you, too early to say), the product described in the person's own terms, and up to three reasons, each citing a line of their style profile or garments they own, plus whether it fills a gap and how many similar pieces they already own. Word the answer yourself; nothing is saved or bought.

tools.name: wardrobe_gaps
tools.description: The core garment classes the signed-in person's wardrobe owns none of (for example footwear), plus how many items they own per class. Use it before recommending anything to buy.

tools.name: create_saved_outfit
tools.description: Save an outfit to the signed-in person's wardrobe from item ids they own, typically the ids suggest_outfit just returned. Give it a short name (e.g. 'Client dinner'). Works only once the person has turned on 'Allow assistants to change my wardrobe' under Profile → Connected assistants in the Alama app; otherwise it refuses and nothing is saved. Free accounts have a saved-outfit limit, shared with the app. Never deletes or changes an existing outfit.

tools.name: add_want
tools.description: Record that the signed-in person wants an outside product, usually right after does_it_suit_me. Pass the product page link, a link to its picture, or its description (pass the description too when you have it), and an optional short note. The product is described in the person's own wardrobe terms and saved to their wants, which get_context returns and Alama uses to look for it. Nothing is bought. Works only once the person has turned on 'Allow assistants to change my wardrobe' under Profile → Connected assistants in the Alama app; otherwise it refuses and nothing is saved. Asking twice the same day does not save it twice.

tools.name: record_signal
tools.description: Record one thing the signed-in person tells you, so their style profile learns from it: 'wore' (a garment they own, by item_id from list_wardrobe), 'bought', 'liked' or 'rejected' (a garment they own by item_id, or an outside product by its link or description). `on` is the day it happened, YYYY-MM-DD, today by default, up to 30 days back. Record only what the person said, never a guess. Works only once the person has turned on 'Allow assistants to change my wardrobe' under Profile → Connected assistants in the Alama app; otherwise it refuses and nothing is saved. The same thing on the same day is recorded once.

tools.name: add_item
tools.description: Add one item the signed-in person says they own to their wardrobe, from its description (for example 'navy wool coat') or the link to its product page. One call per item. It is filed in Alama's own terms and returned as filed: read `reads_as` back so the person can correct it. The item has no photo yet: when `add_photo_url` is returned, offer it as the way to add one now (a page that needs no app and no sign-in, valid for an hour), or they can photograph it in the Alama app. Add only what the person says they own, never a guess, and never something they are only thinking of buying (use add_want for that). Works only once the person has allowed it: by ticking 'Let assistants add clothes I describe' when connecting Alama, or by turning on 'Allow assistants to change my wardrobe' under Profile → Connected assistants in the Alama app; otherwise it refuses and says how. Free accounts can hold a limited number of items without a photo, and there is a daily limit; when one is reached it refuses and says so. Never deletes or changes an existing item.

tools.name: list_saved_outfits
tools.description: The outfits the signed-in person has saved in Alama, most recently changed first, each with its `outfit_id`, its name and the items in it. Use it when they refer to an outfit they already have ('my Friday outfit', 'the look I saved last week'), or before try_on to find the `outfit_id`. `query` matches a word in the outfit's name. Paged: pass `next_cursor` back as `cursor`. Changes nothing.

tools.name: try_on
tools.description: Get a link where the signed-in person sees their own clothes on them. Pass `outfit_id` for a saved outfit (ids come from list_saved_outfits or create_saved_outfit), or `item_ids` for a look that is not saved (for example the items suggest_outfit returned, or a single item). Returns `try_on_url`: give it to the person exactly as returned, including everything after the `?`, because the page cannot open without it. On that page they add a full-length photo of themselves and Alama makes the picture, the same try-on as in the Alama app; it is also saved to their try-ons there. The link works for one hour. You never receive the photo or the picture, so do not ask the person to send you a photo and do not draw the look yourself. Items without a photo are left out and listed in `skipped`, each with a link to add one. Try-ons have a daily allowance; `allowance` says what is left. Changes nothing in the wardrobe.
